problem: Pre-trained V&L BERTs had been used in VLN only as instruction encoders (PRESS, PREVALENT) or as path-instruction compatibility scorers for beam search (VLN-BERT). They were not used as the navigator itself, because a stateless BERT cannot handle the history-dependent, partially observable decision process. Self-attending over long instruction and trajectory sequences at every step is also too memory-hungry to train.
motivation: V&L BERTs pre-trained on large image-text corpora capture generic visual-textual correspondence, which VLN needs. VLN agents, however, stacked complex encoder-decoder models (LSTM state, cross-modal attention modules) on top of such features and could not fully exploit the pre-trained knowledge. The authors observe that BERT's own tokens and attention can carry recurrent state and produce action scores, so the whole navigator can be a single fine-tuned BERT.
key_idea: Add recurrence to a pre-trained V&L BERT by treating the [CLS] output as an agent state token that is fed back as the leading input token at every step, alongside the once-encoded instruction (keys/values only) and the current candidate-view tokens, and read the action (and object) probabilities directly from the final-layer state-to-visual attention weights.
insight: The gain comes from using the pre-trained BERT as the entire navigator rather than as a feature extractor. In Table 3 (R2R val-unseen SR), frozen BERT as language encoder drops SR from 49.81 (EnvDrop baseline) to 44.15, and frozen BERT as language+vision encoder drops it to 30.74; fine-tuned, these give 52.11 and 54.75. Adding the recurrent state gives 55.21, attention-as-decision 57.22, and cross-modal matching 58.71 SR / 53.41 SPL. Initialisation matters a lot (random init 50 vs OSCAR 59 vs PREVALENT 63 val-unseen SR), and reward shaping adds only marginally (58.32→58.71). Encoding language only once is a memory/batch-size trade-off rather than strictly better: it runs batch 16 in 9.2GB versus batch 6 in 11GB. With gradient accumulation to batch 16, per-step re-attention of raw embeddings (Emb-Attn) actually beats it on val-unseen (61.00 vs 58.71 SR), while re-attending previous-step language outputs (Re-Attn) degrades badly. On PREVALENT, cross-modal matching slightly helps unseen (62.07→62.75 SR) but hurts seen (76.79→72.18).
method: Recurrent state token: at t=0 the instruction [CLS]+U+[SEP] is encoded by the BERT; the [CLS] output becomes the initial state s0. At each step the previous state is the leading token of the input sequence, and its updated output (after refinement) becomes the next step's state. There is no LSTM or memory buffer.

Language-once encoding: instruction token features from initialisation are reused at every step, acting only as keys/values (not queries), similar to LXMERT's cross-modality encoder. This cuts training memory so the model trains on one 11GB GPU with batch 16.

Visual tokens: each candidate navigable view is a ResNet-152 (Places365) 2048-d feature concatenated with a 128-d heading/elevation encoding and linearly projected; a zero vector serves as the STOP token. In REVERIE, Faster-RCNN (Visual Genome) object features with box-position and direction encodings are added as extra tokens.

Attention-as-decision: action probabilities are the final-layer state-to-visual attention scores, averaged over 12 heads and softmaxed (VisualBERT-style). Object grounding uses the same scores over object tokens. In REVERIE the agent stops when any object token scores above all scene tokens and grounds the top-scoring object.

State refinement: raw text and visual tokens are pooled with the state's final-layer attention weights, fused by element-wise product (visual-only in REVERIE), concatenated with the state output and projected. The directional encoding of the chosen action is then concatenated and projected to form s_t.

Training: IL (teacher forcing, cross-entropy) is mixed with A2C RL (MLP critic on the state), using progress reward plus nDTW path-fidelity reward and a penalty for overshooting the target. REVERIE adds an object-grounding cross-entropy loss. Optimisation uses AdamW at lr 1e-5 on a single 2080Ti.

Backbone adaptation: initialised from OSCAR (one-stream, without object tags), or from PREVALENT (LXMERT-like). For PREVALENT the language branch of the cross-modality encoder is removed, the state is concatenated with visual tokens, and the EnvDrop downstream network is dropped.

setting.backbone: OSCAR-initialised one-stream V&L BERT or PREVALENT-initialised LXMERT-like transformer (fine-tuned end-to-end as the navigator); ResNet-152 (Places365) and Faster-RCNN (Visual Genome) frozen feature extractors
setting.model_size: BERT-base scale (12 layers, 12 heads); parameter count not stated
setting.training_data: R2R: original train set plus PREVALENT's augmented data (300k iterations, batch 16). REVERIE: REVERIE train (200k iterations, batch 8). Weights initialised from OSCAR (generic image-text pre-training) or PREVALENT (VLN-specific image-text-action pre-training); no new pre-training by the authors.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (precomputed ResNet-152 features of the candidate navigable views with heading/elevation encoding); plus Faster-RCNN features of benchmark-provided object boxes in REVERIE
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (panoramic candidate selection + STOP); object selection among candidates in REVERIE
setting.privileged: none (REVERIE uses the benchmark-provided candidate object bounding boxes, standard for that task)

numbers_note: Table 1 (R2R) prints integer SR/SPL; the appendix tables give 2-decimal values for the same models on the val splits. For init. OSCAR (Table 3 'Full model', Table 6): val-seen SR 71.11, SPL 67.23, OSR 76.79; val-unseen SR 58.71, SPL 53.41, OSR 65.86. For init. PREVALENT with matching (Tables 5/6): val-seen SR 72.18, SPL 67.72, OSR 78.16; val-unseen SR 62.75, SPL 56.84, OSR 70.24. The appendix also reports a PREVALENT variant without cross-modal matching: val-seen SR 76.79, SPL 73.13; val-unseen SR 62.07, SPL 56.15. All results are single-run (greedy, no beam search, no pre-exploration). Learning curves are shown only in a figure.
results: Initialised from PREVALENT, the model reaches 63 SR / 57 SPL on R2R test-unseen (63/57 on val-unseen). The strongest prior single-run agents were RelGraph (55/52) and PREVALENT+EnvDrop (54/51), so this is about +8 SR. Initialised from OSCAR it already gets 57/53 on test-unseen. On REVERIE test-unseen the PREVALENT-initialised model gets 29.61 SR, 23.99 SPL, 16.50 RGS and 13.51 RGSPL, versus FAST-MATTN's 19.88/11.61/11.28/6.08; FAST-MATTN keeps a higher OSR (30.63 vs 32.91 is reversed only for the PREVALENT variant) because of much longer trajectories. A single network handles both navigation and remote object grounding.
limitations: Encoding language only once is mainly a memory compromise: with gradient accumulation to the same batch size, per-step language self-attention (Emb-Attn) outperforms it on R2R val-unseen (61.00 vs 58.71 SR), so the design may be suboptimal given more compute.

Navigation history is compressed into a single recurrent state token, and only precomputed features of candidate views on the discrete Matterport3D nav-graph are used; evaluation covers single-run R2R/REVERIE only (no continuous environments, no real robot).
Training is slow on the old simulator (about 7 days for 600k iterations with OSCAR init), and gains rely heavily on the initialisation (random init drops R2R val-unseen SR from 59 to 50).
